questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.

questions.question: After a trip:

options.text: A vehicle should be placed out-of-service.
A vehicle's oil should be changed.
A vehicle's after-trip inspection should be completed.
A vehicle's battery should be disconnected.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle's after-trip inspection should be completed.
questions.explanation: After each trip, you must complete an inspection of each vehicle you drove and file a report.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it means:

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, there is a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Operating an unsafe vehicle is illegal under federal and state laws.

questions.question: If your trailer begins to jackknife while driving, you should not:

options.text: Allow the trailer to straighten out.
Allow the wheels to grip the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer starts to jackknife, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels regain grip on the road. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Applying brakes is what locked the wheels in the first place.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.correctAnswerText: Bug-eye
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved convex mirrors called "bug-eye" mirrors. They show a wider view than flat mirrors but make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: To help prevent rollovers, you should:

options.text: Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, load cargo as low as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: When driving a trailer with ABS, you should:

options.text: Not press the brakes as hard as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make the ABS activate.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Try to brake less often than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a truck-trailer with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would if the vehicle did not have ABS.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum leakage is 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle should not be driven and needs repairs.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, you should:

options.text: Not worry because another vehicle will likely hit it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when you see objects in your lane. Even a cardboard box might contain heavy items that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release them until the wheels roll, then repeat.
Apply the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Apply the emergency brake until the vehicle starts to slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release them until the wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking for emergencies means pushing the brakes fully until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: After starting the engine, how long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds after the engine starts. Never drive if oil pressure is too low.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation that might happen.
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation that might happen.
questions.explanation: Check the road ahead often for hazards. Always have a plan for dealing with dangers you might see.

questions.question: Which statement about distracted driving is true?

options.text: It only comes from physical distraction, never mental distraction.
Pre-programming radio stations can increase it.
Eating while driving helps avoid it.
It can be reduced by avoiding complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be reduced by avoiding complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid complex or emotional conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you drive and don't eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains in the storage tanks to remove water and compressor oil. If these are not removed, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope it goes away.
Write a report that describes your concerns.
Avoid that part and hope nobody notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report that describes your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day of driving, you should write a report about any vehicle issues. Note any problems that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is not working properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may exit the rear of the muffler.
It may cause problems if the trailer is loaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can allow poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper area. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you don't get enough sleep.
When you want to take a nap.
The time needed to prepare before driving after sleep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you don't get enough sleep.
questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you don't sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light in air brake vehicles is usually red. It may also have a buzzer.
